FOREWORD

This Indian Standard (Second Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Hosiery Sectional Committee, had been approved by the Textile Division Council. This standard was tirst published in1980 and revised in 1991. It has been again revised on the basis of experience gained in its implementation. Foilowing are the major changes carried out in this revision: a) Constructional requirements for extra super fine variety of single jersy cloth have been introduced; and counces/dm for Coarse `A', fine and superfine varieties of knitted fabric

b) Requirement of wales/din have been modified; and c) Requirement The composition

pH value of aquous extract has been modified. responsible for formulation of this standard is given in Annex C.

of the Committee

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2: 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

IS 9469:2003

Indian Standard TEXTILES --FABRIC, COTTON, PLAIN (SINGLE JERSEY) KNITTED -- SPECIFICATION (Second
1 SCOPE 1. I This standard prescribes the requirements of grey, scoured, bleached, dyed or printed plain (single jersey) knitted fabric, that is, fabric knitted in plain stitches on circular looms. 1.2 This standard also covers coloured plain knitted cotton fabric obtained by knitting the fabric with dyed yarn. 1.3 This standard does not specify the general appearance, feel, lusture, whiteness or shade of knitted fabric (see also 5.4). 2 REFERENCES The standards given in Annex A contain provisions which through reference in this text, constitute provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid. All standards are subject to revision, and parties to agreements based on this standard are encouraged tc investigate the possibility of applying the most recent editions of the standards indicated in Annex A. 3 TERMINOLOGY For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given in IS 3596 shall apply (see also SP 45). 4 MANUFACTURE 4.1 The tubular fabric shall be evenly knitted in plain stitches. The width of tubular fabric shall be uniform throughout and shall correspond to the diameter of the knitting machine. The fabric shall not be over boarded or pulled in length while calendering. If required by the b..yer, the bleached fabric may also be treated with blueing/optical whitening agents. The fabric may also be printed with motifs or designs if desired by the buyer. 4.2 The fabric shall be free from knitting defects such as ladders, dropped stitches, holes, cuts and mends and chemical defects, such as, defective bleaching in case of bleached fabric; streaks, stains and uneven dyeing in case of dyed fabric; and defective printing in case of printed fabric. 5 REQUIREMENTS 5.1 Yarn The yarn used in knitting the fabric shall conform to 1

Revision)
IS 834. Supertine and extra superfine (see Table fabrics shall be knitted from combed yam only. 5.2 Constructional requirements shall be as given in Table 1. 1)

of plain knitted fabric

5.3 The fabric shall also conform to other requirements given in Table 2. 5.4 Sealed Sample In order to illustrate or specify the indeterminable characteristics, such as, general appearance, degree of whiteness, colour, shade or print design of fabric, a sample has been agreed upon and sealed, the supply shall be in conformity with the sample in such respects. 5.4.1 The custody of the sealed sample shall be a matter of prior agreement between the buyer and the seller. 6 MARKING 6.1 Each roll of fabric following information: a) Name of material; b) Count of yam and type (carded or combed); c) Designation of fabric; d) Diameter of knitting machine; e) Indication of source of manufacture; f) Washing instructions, if any; and g) Any other information or the law in force. 6.2 BIS Certification as required by the buyer shall be marked with the

Marking

The roll may also be marked with the Standard Mark. 6.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau ofIrrdian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The details of conditions under whi$h the license for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 7 PACKING The fabric shall be well packed and supplied in a clean and dry state free from stains, greases, etc, preferably in accordance with IS 3086 or IS 3325 as the case may be.

standard shall be determined on the basis of the tests carried on samples selected from the lot. 8.2 Unless otherwise agreed to between the buyer and the seller, a number of rolls depending upon the size of the lot shall be selected at random from the lot to constitute the gross sample. In any consignment all rolls knitted on a particular diameter of knitting machine having same designation and knitted from type (carded or combed) and count of yarn and delivered to a buyer against one dispatch note shall constitute a lot.

13-1.1 The test specimens shall be tested in prevailing. In case of dispute, the samples shall be conditioned and tested in the standard atmosphere as given in IS 6359. B-2 DIMENSIONAL RELAXATION) B-2.1

B-2.2

Procedure

CHANGES

(DUE TO

of Test Specimens

B-2. 1.1 Take a roll of fabric from the test sample (see Note l). Cut a piece measuring approximately 30 cm x full width. Mark the direction of wales and courses in the test specimen. Mark centrally on the test specimen, by means of indelible ink or a fast dyed cotton sewing thread, an area of 15 cm x 15 cm with two or its sides in the direction of wales and the other two in t!le direction of course. Spread this test specimen on a flat smooth surface, carefully remove by hand all creases and wrinkles. Within this area, mark six pairs of marks, three pairs each in the wales direction and the courses direction in such way that the distance between each pair of marks is the same. 4

B-2.2.1 Place the test specimen and spread it on a flat smooth surface. Carefully remove by hand all creases and wrinkles without distorting the test specimen. Measure, correct to the nearest millitnetre, the distance between each pair of marks separately. B-2.2.2 Lay the test specimen flat in a tray of suitable size and having a depth of minimum 10 cm. Soak it under a head of 25 mm of water containing 0.5 percent suitable wetting agent at room temperature for 2 h. Drain out the water and remove the test specimen carefully so that it is not stretched and lay it flat on a smooth surface. Remove the excess of water by absorbent material and dry it at room temperature. B-2.2.3 After drying, condition the test specimen to moisture equilibrium at rootn temperature. Place it on the glass plate, carefully remove all wrinkles and creases and place the other glass plate on the test specimen.

IS 9469:2003 Measure correct to the nearest millimetre, the distance between each pair of marks separately. B-2.3 Calculation Calculate, separately, the percentage of B-2,3.1 dimensional change both in the direction of wales and in the direction of courses by the following formula :

B-3. 1 Take a specimen and lay it flat on a table. Remove all wrinkles and creases without distorting it. On one side of the test specimen, count with the help of a pick glass or magnifying glass, the number of wales and courses in 10 cm at three different places in the test specimen and calculate the average number of wales and courses per dm.
NOI'E -- in case of vests or similar garments, the wales and courses shall be determined in similar manner as for rolls of knitted fabrics.

the distance between a pair of marks (along the wales or courses as the case may be) before soaking; and the distance between the same pair of marks after soaking. B-2.3.2 Calculate separately the dimensional change between all the three pairs of marks in the direction of wales and in the direction of courses and calculate the average dimensional change in each direction.

B-4 MEASUREMENT AQUEOUS EXTRACT

OF /JH VALUE

OF

B-4.1 Take a sample of approximately 2 g of the fabric and cut it into small fragments. Check the pH of the aqueous extract with apH paper of suitable range having gradation of 0.5. Also carry out a blank test on distilled water to check ifpH of the distilled water used is 7. If pH of distilled water is not 7, correction to pH of aqueous extract of test sample shall be applied accordingly.
